name: ANITA payload

placements.quote: ANITA-LITE launched December 17, 2003 ... The ANtarctic Impulsive Transient Antenna (ANITA) ... completed its fourth flight in December 2016
placements.note: This placement records the balloon LAUNCH site only, not a detection location. ANITA is a balloon payload: it takes its actual data at float altitude (~37 km) drifting over the Antarctic continent during each multi-week flight, not at any fixed ground position. Per the brief's guidance for balloon experiments, the site is recorded as the sourced launch facility with this caveat rather than left entirely unplaced, since a real, sourced launch location exists.

technology.value: Balloon-borne array of quad-ridged horn antennas detecting radio-frequency Askaryan-effect pulses from neutrino- and cosmic-ray-induced showers in Antarctic ice
technology.quote: Flying at 120,000ft (~37 km), the instrument observes ~1.5 million square kilometers of ice.

intervals.label: ANITA-LITE
intervals.quote: ANITA-LITE launched December 17, 2003 and flew for ~18.5 days

intervals.label: ANITA-I
intervals.quote: ANITA I launched December 15, 2006, and flew for ~35 days

intervals.label: ANITA-II
intervals.quote: ANITA II launched December 21, 2008, from Williams Field, Antarctica.

intervals.label: ANITA-III
intervals.quote: The third flight of ANITA (ANITA-III) was launched in December 2014 and completed a 22-day flight.

intervals.label: ANITA-IV
intervals.quote: completed its fourth flight in December 2016, after 28 days of flight time

intervals.label: retired
intervals.quote: PUEO leverages experience from and supersedes the successful Antarctic Impulsive Transient Antenna (ANITA) program.

area.quote: the instrument observes ~1.5 million square kilometers of ice

notes: Placement caveat repeated here from experiment:anita: the launch site is not the detection location.

summary.plain: A ring of radio antennas hanging beneath a giant NASA balloon, floating 37 kilometres over Antarctica and listening for the radio crackle of a neutrino hitting the ice far below.
summary.technical: Balloon-borne quad-ridged horn antenna array for Askaryan-effect radio detection of UHE neutrinos and cosmic rays, flown at ~37 km altitude over Antarctica across five flights (2003-2016), launched from the NASA LDB facility near McMurdo Station.
